key_insight: A ~150 μm thin single-crystal organometal halide perovskite can directly detect hundreds-of-MeV charged particles, expanding perovskite radiation sensing beyond X-rays and low-energy particles.
engineering_relevance: The device path is attractive for pixelated, possibly curved high-energy tracking systems because perovskites can be grown directly on electronics without expensive bump-bonding.
method: Thin single-crystal OMHP grown on a patterned substrate using a dewetting technique
Dedicated readout electronics designed to match the crystal time response
Evaluation of response across a high dynamic range of incident particle fluxes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the first demonstration of thin OMHP single crystals detecting high-energy charged particles in the hundreds-of-MeV range, with operation over a wide flux range.
watch_item: Performance is shown from the abstract only, so long-term radiation tolerance, calibration stability, and pixel-level uniformity still need careful validation.
paper_title: Thin single-crystal perovskite detector for high-energy charged particles
